rationale: B wins because it is a little cleaner about conditional proof and does not turn an unknown into a fact. A's category angle says blood pressure is "a feature nobody has cleared," which the update does not establish; B's catch-up angle keeps the rival comparison tighter with "Whoop finally ships the ECG its rivals already have." B still needs a red pencil on "What Whoop's cardiologists actually signed off on," but its proof gate is sharper: "Without the numbers this angle dies."
gaps_in_A: "a feature nobody has cleared" is invented. The update says competitors already ship FDA-cleared ECG; it says nothing about cleared blood-pressure products.
"cuff-free blood pressure" overstates the supplied facts. The update says a non-medical wellness estimate that requires one-time cuff calibration, not a cleared cuffless product.

"How Whoop's cardiologist advisory board shaped the product" gets refused instead of being rebuilt into a conditional clinical-evidence angle. The board alone is fluff, but validation data and advisory-board disclosure are real proof questions.

"Run the detector first" is a soft next step for a launch peg that already exists. The founder needs journalist-fit-check plus pricing, validation, and labeling proof before chasing a fabricated external hook.
gaps_in_B: "What Whoop's cardiologists actually signed off on" overclaims. The update says the advisory board reviewed the features; review is not sign-off.
"downstream load it puts on clinics: false positives, worried-well referrals" imports plausible clinical concerns as premises without supplied evidence. Keep them as questions unless Whoop has data.
"Story type: defensive-comment" is the wrong wrapper. The tier angle is a pricing/access story, not a crisis posture.
"and a cuff is still required to use the blood-pressure half" buries one of the sharpest consumer-accountability angles as a clause instead of making it a standalone story.
